improving, developing, or enhancing its value and utility,
including the provision of serviced stands, housing units,
or commercial sites for sale, lease, or other disposal to
individuals, entities, or institutions;

“licensed electricity utility” refers to the Zimbabwe
Electricity Transmission & Distribution Company
(Private) Limited, the sole owner of electricity backbone
infrastructure in Zimbabwe, in accordance with the
Electricity Act [Chapter 13:19];

 “low voltage network” refers to the electricity distribution
network of line voltages below 0.25 kilovolts;

“medium voltage network” refers to the electricity distribution
network of line voltages between 0.25 kilovolts and 0.65
kilovolts;

“standard connection” refers to a connection to the electricity
supply network where existing high voltage or medium
voltage mains are available within reasonable proximity
and no immediate construction of additional backbone
infrastructure is required.
Application

3. These regulations shall apply to all local authorities, land
developers, and independent distribution licensees.
S.I. 128 of 2026
1789
Objects

4. The objectives of these regulations are to—

(a)	 regulate and facilitate the development of electricity
infrastructure within new or expanding property
developments, ensuring that all electrical works
undertaken by land developers meet approved technical,
safety, and operational standards; and

(b)	 provide a framework for the integration of new
developments into the national electricity grid, including
procedures for connection approval, inspection, and
certification of developer-installed infrastructure by the
licensed transmission or distribution utility; and

(c) define the roles, responsibilities, and obligations of land
developers undertaking the financing, installation, and
commissioning of electricity infrastructure within new
subdivisions, housing estates, industrial parks, or other
developments; and

(d)	 promote public–private collaboration in electricity
network expansion by enabling developers to construct
distribution infrastructure at their own cost under
approved specifications; and

(e)	 protect consumers and the public interest by ensuring
that all electricity infrastructure installed by developers
is—

(i)	 compliant with national electrical codes and safety
standards;

(ii)  designed and installed by qualified and licensed
professionals; and

(iii) subject to testing, verification, and certification
before energisation or grid connection;

and

(f)
establish procedural requirements for the submission,
approval, and registration of developer-installed
electricity networks, including timelines for inspection,
certification, and the conditions under which such
1790
Electricity (Provision of Backbone Infrastructure) Regulations, 2026
infrastructure may be vested in, or transferred to, the
licensed utility; and

(g) support orderly urban and rural electrification, ensuring
that electricity infrastructure developed by private actors
aligns with national energy planning objectives, grid
expansion priorities, and environmental standards.
Provision of electricity backbone infrastructure

5. (1) Every land developer shall be required to provide electricity
backbone infrastructure as an essential component of the services to
be rendered to all stands or properties earmarked to enhance its value
and primary distribution licensee.

(2) The electricity backbone infrastructure shall include, but
is not limited to—

(a)	 medium and low voltage distribution lines;

(b)	 transformers;

(c) mini-substations or feeder pillars where applicable;

(d) service connection points and metering-ready interfaces;

(e)	 trenching and cable laying:

(f)
 protective structures; and

(g)	  any other ancillary works necessary to ensure safe and
reliable electricity supply.

(3) Every land developer within an area where a local authority
provides roads, water and sewerage infrastructure, shall be required
at their own development costs to source the necessary materials and
construct the electricity backbone infrastructure.

(4) All electricity backbone infrastructure works shall be
integrated into the approved layout plan submitted to the local
authority, coordinated with the licensed electricity utility (utility) to
ensure compatibility with existing or planned grid infrastructure prior
to commissioning and handover to the primary distribution licensee.

(5) The cost of providing electricity backbone infrastructure
shall not be recoverable from the utility and shall be borne entirely
by the land developer as part of the development obligations.
S.I. 128 of 2026
1791

(6) Failure to comply with the provisions of this section shall
render the development non-compliant and subject to enforcement
measures, including but not limited to—

(a)	 suspension or revocation of the development permit;

(b)	 withholding of rates clearance or subdivision approval;
and

(c) penalties as specified under these regulations.
Transfer of ownership

6.	 (1) Upon completion of the electricity backbone infrastructure,
and subject to successful inspection and certification by the utility,
the land developer shall, at no cost to the utility transfer ownership
of the electricity backbone infrastructure to the primary distribution
licensee.

(2) The primary distribution licensee shall assume full
responsibility for the operation and maintenance of the electricity
backbone infrastructure from the date of formal handover and
commissioning.

(3) The land developer shall provide a warranty for the
electricity backbone infrastructure for a period of five years from the
date of commissioning.

(4) The inspection referred to in subsection (1) shall be
conducted by the utility or its appointed representative within fourteen
working days of notification of completion by the land developer,
and a formal certificate of acceptance shall be issued upon successful
inspection.
Obligations of land developer

7. (1) Every land developer undertaking electrical infrastructure
development shall—

(a)	 notify the primary distribution licensee in writing of
any proposal to undertake any electrical infrastructure
development attaching Surveyor-General’s approved
proposed stands layout maps (both physical copies and
Geographical Information System (GIS) soft copy in
1792
Electricity (Provision of Backbone Infrastructure) Regulations, 2026
prescribed format) and shall obtain approvals from the
primary distribution licensee prior to commencing the
development activity;

(b)	 acquire and register appropriate wayleaves and easements
from the relevant authorities for overhead power
lines, underground cables, distribution fused pillars,
underground distribution pillars, substations and any
other relevant infrastructure required in consultation
with the primary distribution licensee on newly created
lots with the Deeds Office;

(c) 	 ensure that all design, installation, and construction
work related to the electricity backbone infrastructure
are carried out only by consultants and contractors who
are registered with the primary distribution licensee;

(d) 	 in the event that the land developer fails to meet the
technical, procedural, or safety requirements necessary
for the energisation of the backbone infrastructure, the
responsibility for regularising the works shall rest solely
with the land developer (all associated costs shall be
borne by the developer, and no reimbursement shall be
claimed from the primary distribution licensee).

(2) No stand or property within the development shall be
sold, leased, or otherwise disposed of until the land developer has
demonstrated full compliance with these regulations.
Obligations of primary distribution licensee

8. The primary distribution licensee shall—

(a)	 undertake assessments of any proposed development
to determine electricity infrastructure requirements and
alignment with existing grid capacity;

(b)	 support the land developer in acquiring all necessary
wayleaves and servitudes from the local authority or
other relevant bodies;

(c)	 prepare and approve electrical backbone infrastructure
designs, technical specifications, bills of quantities, and
cost estimates in accordance with approved engineering
standards and any statutory requirements;
S.I. 128 of 2026
1793

(d) 	 review and issue formal approvals to land developers
prior to commencement of any electricity infrastructure
works;

(e) 	 inspect and approve the works being carried out by the
contractor or consultant in construction of the backbone
infrastructure in accordance with relevant primary
distribution licensee guidelines;

(f)
assume full responsibility for the operation and
maintenance of the electricity backbone infrastructure
upon formal transfer of ownership from the land
developer.
Obligations of local authorities

9. (1) A local authority shall, upon receipt of a complete
application from a land developer, assess the proposed development
for compliance with the requirements of these regulations.

(2) Where the local authority is satisfied that the land developer
has met all prescribed conditions, it shall issue a development permit
authorising the commencement or continuation of the development.

(3) A local authority shall maintain a register of all development
permits issued under these regulations and shall share such information
with the primary distribution licensee and other relevant authorities
to facilitate infrastructure planning and service delivery.

(4) In cases of non-compliance by the land developer, the
local authority shall have the power to suspend, revoke, or withhold
the development permit until corrective measures are undertaken by
the land developer.
Obligations of stand or property owner

10. Every individual stand or property owner shall be responsible
for the payment of the approved electricity connection fees as
determined by the primary distribution licensee.
Subdivision and consolidation

11. (1) Any overhead or underground electricity supply crossing
the new property boundaries in view of subdividing or consolidating an
1794
Electricity (Provision of Backbone Infrastructure) Regulations, 2026
existing serviced lot or area with existing multiple power services shall
be removed or rerouted with the approval of the primary distribution
licensee.

(2) The cost of carrying out such works referred to in subsection
(1) and related modification to the existing network infrastructure
shall be borne by the initiating party.
Independent distribution licensee

12. (1) Subject to these regulations and such other terms and
conditions as the Authority may fix in the licence, an independent
distribution licence may authorise for private sector companies to
reticulate unserved areas.

(2) The licensing shall be done through a competitive bidding
procurement process as per the procurement framework outlined in
the Schedule and the Authority shall be responsible for the process.

(3) Independent distribution shall include metering, billing,
operation and maintenance of the infrastructure.

(4) The independent distribution licensee can procure
electricity from the primary transmission or distribution licensee at
bulk supply, IPPs or investing in generation (generation license will
be required) to supply their respective areas.

(5) The independent distribution license shall have a renewable
tenure of twenty-five years subject to renewal conditions.

(6) Where the independent distribution licensee fails to renew
or complete the tenure of the licence—

(a) the primary distribution licensee shall have the first right
of refusal; and

(b)	 in the event that the primary distribution licensee is not
in the position to take over, the transfer shall be through
a competitive bidding; and

(c)	 the competitive bidding process shall be as determined
by the Authority; and

(d)	 the infrastructure shall go through valuation to determine
the value which shall be approved by the Authority.
S.I. 128 of 2026
1795
Operational obligations

13. (1) Every independent distribution licensee shall—

(a)	 manage, operate and maintain their infrastructure—

(i)	 to ensure a safety of their employees and members
of public; and

(ii) reliable flow of electricity;

	 and

(b) 	 be responsible for connecting new customers to the
network and addressing local outages and faults within
approved guaranteed performance standards; and

(c) 	 be responsible for the development and submission to
the Authority consumer protection standards focusing
on customer services and connection procedures.

(2) All independent distribution licensees shall comply
with existing grid and distribution codes, guidelines, standard tariff
structures, and harmonised investment frameworks that support grid
expansion for universal service at fair cost.
Costing and tariffs

14. (1) Costs shall be contained with long-term operational
efficiency and maintenance goals, to protect consumers from over-
investment.

(2) End-user tariffs for electricity supplied by the independent
distribution licensee shall not exceed the standard tariffs set for the
primary distribution licensee, with approval and oversight from the
Authority.
Service connection

15. (1) Connection fees and guidelines shall be determined by
the distribution licensee and approved by the Authority.

(2) An individual in need of electricity service connection
shall pay the approved connection fees for the installation of the
meter and connection of power supply.
1796
Electricity (Provision of Backbone Infrastructure) Regulations, 2026
Standard connections

16. Where existing high voltage (HV) or medium voltage
(MV) mains infrastructure is available within reasonable proximity
to a development site, and supply can be extended without the need
for immediate construction of additional backbone infrastructure,
the primary distribution licensee shall apply a standard connection
procedure.
Offences

17. Any person who contravenes the provisions of these
regulations shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not
exceeding level 5 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six
months or to both such fine and such imprisonment.
Schedule (Section 12)
INDEPENDENT DISTRIBUTION LICENSEE PROCUREMENT
Tender committee and adjudication

The tender and adjudication committee shall be chaired by the Authority,
with the ministry responsible for energy and the Zimbabwe Electricity Transmission
Distribution Company being members.

Issuing of tender

The Authority shall flight the tender in terms of a competitive bid document
designed and agreed by the Tender and Adjudication Committee.

The tender window shall be open for a period of thirty days.
Basis of selection or adjudication

(a)
cost to execute the project – based on the design and bill of
quantities (thirty per centum).

(b)
technical capacity and competence (forty per centum).

(c)
financial capacity (thirty per centum).
S.I. 128 of 2026
1797
Licensing

Once a company has been selected through the competitive tendering process,
the Authority shall proceed to issue the independent distribution licence to that
selected bidder.
Conditions of licence

The following are the general licence conditions for independent electricity
distribution—

(a)
tenure – renewable twenty-five years;

(b)
financial close to be attained in a period less than six months;

(c)
project to be executed (after financial close) in a period less than
twelve months;

(d)
licensee must have customer charter approved by the Authority;

(e)
licensee shall abide by the distribution code.

1798
Electricity (Provision of Backbone Infrastructure) Regulations, 2026
Supplement to the Zimbabwean Government Gazette dated the 31st July, 2026.

Statutory Instrument 119 of 2026.
[CAP. 13.19
Electricity (Minimum Energy Performance Standards for
Appliances and Labelling) Regulations, 2026

IT is hereby notified that the Minister of Energy and Power
Development, after consultation with the Authority, in terms of section
65 of the Electricity Act [Chapter 13:19], has made the following
regulations:—
Title

1. These regulations may be cited as the Electricity (Minimum
Energy Performance Standards for Appliances and Labelling)
Regulations, 2026.
Interpretation

2. In these regulations—
“appliance” means a device, machine or piece of equipment that
uses electricity to perform a specific function;

“label” means a label of an appliance which contains product
information, including energy performance;

“accredited testing facility” means a laboratory that has been
formally recognised by the Authority as technically
competent to perform specific tests, measurements, or
calibrations.
Application

3. These regulations shall apply to importers, manufacturers,
distributors, and retailers that supply appliances.

Registration of manufacturers and importers of appliances

4. (1) Every manufacturer or importer of appliances listed in the
First Schedule shall register with the Authority.
(2) The Authority shall keep a register containing all
information that indicates—
(a)
appliances that are compliant with the applicable
minimum electricity performance standards (MEPS)
and all related certificates of conformity; and
(b)
details of the manufacturer or importer.
(3) The registration shall be in a form specified in the Second
Schedule.

5. (1) No person shall import, manufacture, store, offer for sale,
sell, distribute, or receive as a donation an appliance listed in the First
Schedule unless it complies with the MEPS requirements provided
for each appliance.

(2) The standards and requirements referred to in subsection

fine and such imprisonment.

6. 	 (1) No person shall import, manufacture, store, offer for
sale, sell, distribute, or receive as a donation an appliance unless
the appliance bears a label which indicates the minimum energy
performance.

(2) The label on an appliance shall—

(b)  be written in the English language; and

(c)  be affixed conspicuously on both the appliance and the
package that contains the appliance.

(3) Where the label is affixed on the appliance, it shall be in
colour, printed on a waterproof material and affixed conspicuously
onto the appliance so that it remains clearly visible and is not obscured
whenever the appliance is displayed.

(4) Any supplier, manufacturer or importer of an electrical

(a)  without a label specified in the Third Schedule; or

(b)  who fails to display a label;


shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not

(5) Subject to subsection (4)(a) and (b), a supplier, manufacturer
or importer shall provide an energy performance certificate from an
accredited testing centre and rectify the labelling requirements within
thirty days.
Energy performance conformity certification
7. (1) The manufacturer of appliances listed in the First Schedule
shall ensure that energy performance conformity certification has been
conducted by an accredited testing facility, and such a certificate shall
be made available to the Authority.

(2) No person shall import an electrical appliance without
a consignment-based conformity assessment certificate from an
assessment agent, as defined in the Statutory Instrument 132 of
2015, Control of Goods (Open General Import Licence) (Standards
Assessment) Notice, 2015, indicating the minimum energy performance
standards specified in the First Schedule.

(3) Where an appliance is not provided for in terms of
subsection (2), certification from the country of origin shall be
acceptable if it has been issued by an accredited testing facility.

(4) Any person who contravenes subsections (1), (2) and (3)
shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 5

or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months or to both

(5) The manufacturer or importer in question shall rectify the

8. Disposal of seized appliances shall be as set out in the

IT is hereby notified that the Minister of Energy and Power
Development, after consultation with the Zimbabwe Energy Regulatory
Authority, in terms of section 65 of the Electricity Act [Chapter 13:19],
has made the following regulations:—
Title
1. These regulations may be cited as the Electricity (Energy
Management) Regulations, 2026.
Interpretation
2. In these regulations—
“carbon finance” means a mechanism that facilitates the
financial reward through carbon credits for the reduction
of greenhouse gas emissions by emitters in developing
countries;
“designated facility” means a facility with an installed capacity
of at least 100kVA of or a maximum demand customer
of a distribution licensee;
“energy audit” means an inspection, survey and analysis of
energy flows for energy conservation in a building,
process, or system to reduce the amount of energy input
into the system without negatively affecting the output;
“energy auditor” means a person licensed by the Authority
who carries out inspection, survey and analysis of
energy flows in a building, process, or system to reduce
the amount of energy input into the system without
negatively affecting the output, and includes a firm;
S.I. 122 of 2026
1735

“energy conservation” means the practice of reducing or
foregoing energy consumption to save resources;

“energy consumption rating” means the classification by the
Authority of premises based on the amount of energy
consumed;

“energy efficiency measures” means strategies and techniques
to optimise energy consumption;

“energy investment plan” means the allocation of resources
for the purpose of advancement, capacity growth, and
improvement of energy efficiency and conservation
measures;

“energy management policy” means a formal statement of
intent by the organisation of its overall intentions and
direction related to its energy performance;

“energy manager” means a person licensed by the Authority
who carries out and optimises the energy performance
of a facility, building, or industrial plant;

“energy savings” means the reduction of energy units
consumed per unit of production or per square metre;

“energy service company” means a company or business
registered with the Authority to provides energy solutions
and services including design, implementation and
management of projects on energy management, energy
efficiency and retrofitting;

“facility” includes factories, industries, mines, farms,
commercial buildings, and institutional buildings, plants;

“licensed professional” means a person licensed to carry out
energy audits or energy management or measurement
and verification activities;

“measurement and verification professional” means a person
licensed by the Authority who manages or performs
internationally recognised methods of quantifying the
energy usage impacts of energy management activities;

“testing centre” means an institution or facility authorised
to carry out and validated equipment or machinery for
energy performance.
Electricity (Energy Management) Regulations, 2026
1736
Application
3. These regulations shall apply to all designated facilities.
Energy consumption and facility rating
4. (1) The Authority shall carry out energy consumption and
facility ratings for all designated facilities.

(2) Designated facilities referred to in subsection (1) shall be
classified as specified in the First Schedule according to their energy
consumption, and they shall be recorded in such a manner and form
as specified by the Authority.
Minimum energy performance standards for industrial equipment
5. (1) The minimum energy performance standards set out the
requirements that must be met or exceeded for all the industrial
equipment that is manufactured or imported into Zimbabwe.

(2) No equipment shall be imported, sold, leased or used in
Zimbabwe except where—

(a)	  the energy performance characteristics of the equipment
comply with the standards specified in the Second
Schedule for that equipment range; and

(b) the importer or manufacturer has presented a certificate
of conformity from an authorised testing centre.

(3) The energy performance criteria and testing requirements
are set out in national or internationally adopted standards specified
in the Second Schedule.
Energy management policy
6. (1) The owner or occupier of the designated facility shall
develop an energy management policy for the facility which shall
have the minimum requirements as provided in the Third Schedule
and in adherence to Zimbabwe Standard (ZWS) ISO 50001 series
standard for energy management systems.

(2) The owner or occupier of the designated facility shall file
the energy management policy with the Authority for approval before
implementation.

(3) The filing shall be done within twelve months of
promulgation of these regulations for already existing designated
facilities and before electricity connection for new designated facilities.
S.I. 122 of 2026
1737

(4) The owner or occupier of a designated facility must appoint
an energy manager who shall be responsible for the implementation
of energy management policy, optimising the energy performance,
energy efficiency and conservation measures.

(5) Any person who shall be engaged for energy manager
activities and role must be licensed by the Authority.

(6) The owner or occupier of a designated facility shall cause
the setting up of an Energy Management Committee at the facility,
and the committee must have representations from all levels on the
organisation’s hierarchy.

(7) The owner or occupier of a designated facility must
maintain records of information for a minimum period of five years,
which shall include—

(a)	 daily, weekly, monthly and annual electricity, fuel and
water consumption;

(b)	 daily, weekly, monthly production data or occupancy
levels; and

(c)	 an up-to-date facility plans, infrastructure plans and
floor area drawings.
Energy audits
7. (1) The owner or occupier of a designated facility shall cause
an energy audit of the facility to be undertaken by an energy auditor
at least once every three years.

(2) The energy audits referred to in subsection (1) shall be
carried out in a manner specified by the ZWS ISO 50002 standards
set out in the Fourth Schedule.

(3) The report of the audit undertaken in terms of subsection
(1) shall be in the form set out in the Fifth Schedule.

(4) The Authority may subject the energy audit process to
verification after giving not less than fourteen days’ notice to the
facility owner or occupier.

(5) The owner or occupier shall submit the audit report of the
audit to the Authority in a manner approved by the Authority, within
thirty days of completion of the audit.

(6) An energy auditor shall, upon completion of an audit,
execute a quality assurance declaration in the form set out in the Sixth
Schedule.
Electricity (Energy Management) Regulations, 2026
1738

(7) The Authority shall examine the report submitted in terms
of subsection (5) for approval and monitor the implementation of
energy efficiency measures.

(8) Where the audit is not satisfactory, the Authority shall
cause the audit to be conducted again under supervision.
Energy efficiency investment plan
8. (1) An owner or occupier of designated facilities shall within
three months of the energy audit prepare and submit to the Authority
an energy efficiency investment plan for the next three years, setting
out proposals for the energy efficiency and conservation measures
identified on the energy audit.

(2) An energy efficiency investment plan referred to in
subsection (1) shall be reviewed by the Authority and may be considered
for funding under the revolving energy savings fund.
Energy efficiency measures
9. (1) The owner or occupier of a designated facility shall take
measures to realise at least fifty per centum of the identified and
recommended energy savings opportunities in the energy audit report
and specified in the energy efficiency investment plan within three
years of the energy efficiency investment plan.

(2) An owner or occupier of a designated facility may consider
the inclusion of the relevant components of an energy efficiency
investment plan into a project to be registered under the carbon finance
mechanism which may be in place from time to time.
Implementation reports
10. (1) Every designated facility shall submit an annual
implementation report in the form specified in the Seventh Schedule
within thirty days of year-end in response to energy savings
opportunities.

(2) The Authority shall inspect to verify compliance with the
implementation report.
Energy use returns
11. Every designated facility shall submit energy use returns
within fourteen days of the end of the period quarterly and annually
as provided in the Eighth Schedule.
S.I. 122 of 2026
1739
Measurement and verification
12. (1) No person shall carry out or conduct measurement and
verification of energy efficiency or energy conservation measures
without a valid licence issued in terms of section 15.

(2) The measurement and verification process shall be
conducted as set out in the ZWS ISO 50015 as specified in the Fourth
Schedule, International Performance Measurement and Verification
Protocol and ASHRAE Guideline 14.

(3) The Authority shall set guidelines for the reporting
requirements at the end of a measurement and verification period.

(4) The Authority shall cause measurement and verification
to be performed for every energy efficiency investment plan to be
implemented.
Energy audit by Authority
13. (1) Notwithstanding section 7, the Authority may, after giving
not less than fourteen days’ notice to the facility owner or occupier,
undertake an energy audit at its own cost.

(2) The owner or occupier of the designated facility shall
allow the Authority access to the facility for purposes of such audit.
Disputes
14. (1) In the event of a dispute between a designated facility
owner or occupier and the energy auditor or the energy service
company (ESCO), or the measurement and verification professional,
the parties shall first attempt to resolve the dispute themselves.

(2) Where the parties fail to resolve their dispute, one or more
or the parties to the dispute may petition the Authority providing
relevant documentation concerning—

(a)	 the issues in dispute; and

(b)	 the position of each of the parties with respect to these
issues; and

(c)	 the areas of agreement between the parties if any.


(3) The other parties to the dispute shall be afforded an
opportunity by the Authority to respond to the petition and to provide
any other information which may assist in the resolution of the dispute.
Electricity (Energy Management) Regulations, 2026
1740

(4) The Authority after holding a hearing on the dispute shall
make its determination in the matter.
Licensing of professionals and energy audit firms
15. (1) No person shall carry out an energy audit unless he or she
is licensed as an energy auditor by the Authority.

(2) A person shall be qualified to be licensed by the Authority
as an energy auditor if the person holds the qualifications set out in
the Ninth Schedule.

(3) An organisation shall be licensed as an energy audit or
measurement and verification firm—

(a)	 if it is registered in Zimbabwe; and

(b)	 if it employs at least one licensed professional.

(4) If a company is registered outside of Zimbabwe, the
company shall submit proof of such registration to the Authority and
have in its employment at least one licensed energy auditor.

(5) A person wishing to be licensed as an energy auditor or
an energy audit firm, a measurement and verification professional or
energy managers shall make an application to the Authority in the
form set out in the Ninth Schedule.

(6) The Authority may require an applicant to be examined
in such a manner as it may determine for purposes of ascertaining his
or her ability to undertake, engage in or perform energy management,
energy audit or measurement and verification work.

(7) All licences shall be subject to a payment of a fee specified
in the Tenth Schedule.
Determination of application
16. (1) The Authority shall examine all applications referred to
in section 15, and may—

(a)	 grant the licence accordingly, either without conditions
or subject to such conditions as it may deem fit; or

(b) refuse to grant the licence and give reasons.

(2) A licence shall be valid for three years from the date of
issue.
S.I. 122 of 2026
1741
Renewal and replacement of licences
17. (1) An application for renewal of a licence shall be made at
least thirty days before the expiry date of the existing licence.

(2) If the Authority is satisfied that the applicant has
continuously met the conditions of the current licence, the Authority
shall renew the licence.

(3) If the application for the renewal of a licence has been
made before the expiry of the licence but has not been dealt with by
the Authority when the licence expires, that licence shall remain valid
until the application for renewal is finalised, and any renewal in such
case shall be deemed to have commenced from the day the licence
would have expired before the renewal thereof.

(4) Where, upon application, it is shown to the satisfaction
of the Authority that a licence has been lost, destroyed or defaced the
Authority may issue a duplicate licence.

(5) The Authority shall maintain a register of all licensed
energy auditors, energy audit firms, measurement and verification
professionals, energy managers and the register shall be available
for inspection by the public free of charge.

(6) All licence renewals shall be subject to a payment of a
fee specified in the Tenth Schedule.
Cancellation of licence
18. (1) The Authority may, on its own initiative or upon receiving
a complaint from—

(a)	 any owner or occupier or any industry association
considered by the Authority to be sufficiently
representative of such industry; or

(b) any other licensee or person involved in the energy
audit, or energy management, or measurements and
verification, or ESCO;
conduct an inquiry into the operations of any licensee to determine
its compliance with these regulations.

(2) In conducting an inquiry in terms of subsection (1), the
Authority shall have the same powers, rights and privileges as are
conferred upon a commissioner by the Commissions of Inquiry Act
Electricity (Energy Management) Regulations, 2026
1742
[Chapter 10:07], other than the power to order a person to be detained
in custody, and sections 9 to 13 and 15 to 19 of that Act shall apply
with any such changes as may be necessary in relation to such inquiry.

(3) If, after an inquiry held in terms of subsection (2), the
Authority is satisfied that—

(a) the licensee has contravened any provision of these
regulations; or

(b)	 the licensee has failed to comply with any term or
condition of its licence; or

(c) the financial position of the licensee is such that it is
unable to fully and efficiently discharge the duties and
obligations imposed on it by its licence;
the Authority may cancel the licence.

(4) The Authority shall notify the licensee in writing of the
date and venue of an inquiry under this section and shall allow the
licensee an opportunity to make representations at the inquiry.
Energy service company
19. (1) The Authority shall register ESCOs as set out in the form
in the Eleventh Schedule.

(2) The Authority shall come up with guidelines for the
registration of ESCOs and the guidelines shall be made public and
accessible at any given time.

(3) A register of ESCO’s shall be kept by the Authority listing
the ESCOs’ expertise with regard to energy performance contracting.
Offences
20. Any person who—

(a)	 carries out an energy audit or measurements and
verification or energy management without a valid
licence issued by the Authority; or

(b)	 being the owner or occupier of a designated facility—

 (i)	 fails to submit an audit report to the Authority; or

(ii)	 denies the Authority or its agent access to the facility
for purposes of implementing these regulations;
S.I. 122 of 2026
1743
shall be guilty of an offence and liable to fine not exceeding level
5 or imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months or to both
such fine and such imprisonment.

6. Electric vehicle charging station setup.

Schedule: Standards

IT is hereby notified that the Minister of Energy and Power
Development, after consultation with the Zimbabwe Energy Regulatory
Authority, in terms of section 65 of the Electricity Act [Chapter 13:19],
has made the following regulations:—
Title
1. These regulations may be cited as the Electricity (Electric
Vehicle Charging Station Safety) Regulations, 2026.
Interpretation
2. In these regulations—
DISTRIBUTED BY VERITAS
e-mail: veritas@mango.zw; website: www.veritaszim.net
Veritas makes every effort to ensure the provision of reliable information,
but cannot take legal responsibility for information supplied.
1708
Electricity (Electric Vehicle Charging Station Safety) Regulations, 2026

“alternating current” means a type of electrical current in
which the direction of the flow of electrons switches
back and forth at regular intervals or cycles;

“consignment based conformity assessment” means a
process for ensuring that a consignment to be shipped
into the Zimbabwean market complies with national
standards, relevant international standards, and technical
regulations;

“direct current” means an electric current that is unidirectional
the flow of charge is always in the same direction;

“electric vehicle charging station” refers to a power supply
device that supplies electrical power, be it alternating
current or direct current, for recharging plug-in electric
vehicles;

“electric vehicle” means a vehicle that uses one or more
electric motors for propulsion;

“electric vehicle supply equipment” means any equipment or
electrical component used in charging electric vehicles
at a specific location. Electric vehicle supply equipment
does not include equipment located on the electric
vehicles themselves (on board chargers);

“International Electrotechnical Commission” refers to the
international standards and conformity assessment body
for all fields of electro-technology;

“minimum energy performance standards” specify the
minimum level of energy performance that electric
vehicle charging stations must meet or exceed before
they can be imported, distributed, or offered for sale or
use in Zimbabwe;

“open charge point protocol” means an application protocol
for communication between electric vehicle charging
stations and a central management system also known
as a charging station network;

“residual current device” means a device that is able to detect
a fault current also in the absence of neutral;
S.I. 120 of 2026
1709

“TN-C-S (MEN)” means an earthing system arrangement for
low voltage network that protects people and structures
from electrical hazards;

“ZWS” means the Zimbabwe Standard.
Application

3. These regulations shall apply to all importers and retailers,
contractors, installers, and owners of electric vehicle (EV) charging
stations.
Objects

4. The objectives of these regulations are for the promotion of
electrical safety in the installation and usage of EV charging stations.
Compliance with laws and standards.

5. (1) All EV charging stations must be designed, installed, tested,
certified, inspected, and connected in such a way as to ensure the safety
of the users and the public in accordance with the Electricity (Public
Safety) Regulations, 2018, published in Statutory Instrument 177 of
2018, SAZ ZWS400, SAZ ZWS913:2010.

(2) All EV charging stations must—

(a)  be supplied from a dedicated final sub-circuit; and

(b)	  be supplied from a sub-circuit protected by a voltage-
independent residual current device (RCD) providing
personal protection that is compatible with a charging
supply for an electric vehicle; and

(c)	 provide an earth continuity monitoring system that
disconnects the supply in the event that the earthing
connection to the vehicle becomes ineffective. This
monitoring system must fail to safety; and

(d)	 provide protection against the overload of the charging
supply fittings; and

(e)	 provide protection against the overload of the incoming
supply fittings; and

(f) 	 be supplied from a TNC-S (MEN) system of supply that
includes an earth electrode and MEN connection; and
1710
Electricity (Electric Vehicle Charging Station Safety) Regulations, 2026

(g) 	 be installed so that any socket-outlet of a Mode 3 or
Mode 4 supply is at least 800 mm above the finished
ground level; and

(h)	 for charging stations with multiple connecting points,
all connecting points must be protected by a voltage-
independent RCD that is compatible with a charging
supply for an electric vehicle; and

(i)
all RCDs for the protection of connecting points and
electric vehicle charging stations must incorporate the
ability to continue to protect in the event of above 6mA
of direct current (DC) fault, including leakage, current
or isolate the supply in the event of more than a mA
of DC fault, including leakage, current. Paragraphs (c)
and (g) do not apply to wireless charging stations.

(3) No EV charging station may provide or be connected to
an alternating current (AC) charging supply that—

(a) 	 is not at standard low voltage; and

(b) 	 is not at a nominal frequency of 50 Hertz; and

(c) 	 all functions of an EV charging station must fail to
safety.

(4) Any person offering for sale or supplying an EV charging
station must have, and must make available to the Authority, purchaser,
potential purchaser or installer a supplier declaration of conformity—

(a)	 in respect of an EV charging station complying with
IEC standards, the relevant test reports, approvals or
other document as specified by the Authority; or

(b) 	 in the case of an EV charging station complying with
UL standards, the relevant UL certification verification,
or other document as specified by the Authority.

(5) Any person installing an EV charging station must verify,
keep, and attach to the Certificate of Compliance records that the
EV charging station has been designed, constructed and labelled to
be compatible with a supply of standard low voltage at a nominal
frequency of 50 Hertz.
S.I. 120 of 2026
1711

(6) Any person who contravenes this section shall be guilty
of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level five or to
imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months or to both such
fine and such imprisonment.
Electric vehicle charging station setup

6. (1) Any EV charging station and connected support devices
shall be designed and installed to operate on the Zimbabwe electricity
distribution network and take into consideration the distribution code’s
power quality requirements and installation standard as provided in
the Schedule.

(2) EV charging stations shall include mandated settings
that automatically operate to protect both the customer’s electrical
installation and the distribution network it is connected to, in a bid
to ensure network stability.

(3) EV charging stations shall be provided with protection
against the overload of input supply and output supply fittings.

(4) Where the charging station is to be connected on the
distribution network for commercial purposes—

(a) 	 an EV charging station operator shall notify the
distribution network operator of their intention to set
up such for effective planning; and

(b) 	 the distribution network operator shall assess the impact
the use of the charging station has on the wider electricity
system.

(5) The electric vehicle parking place shall be such that the
connection on the vehicle when parked for charging shall be within
five meters from the electric vehicle charging point.

(6) Where the connection point is installed outdoors, or in a
damp location, the equipment shall have an ingress protection code
at least IP65 as defined in IEC standard 60529.

(7) Hazardous live parts shall not be exposed (this is to protect
persons against electric shock).
1712
Electricity (Electric Vehicle Charging Station Safety) Regulations, 2026

(8) Every part of the electric apparatus shall be securely
guarded and fenced unless they are safe by position or construction.

(9) The electric vehicle charging station shall be equipped
with a protective device against the uncontrolled reverse power flow
from the vehicle.

(10) The electric vehicle charging station shall have protection
to prevent overvoltage or overloading of the battery.

(11) The electric vehicle charging point shall not be energised
until it is connected to the vehicle.

(12) Power supply cables used in charging stations or charging
points shall conform to the manufacturer’s instructions or specifications
or IEC 62893-1 standard.

(13) The safety provisions of all A.C. charging stations shall
be in accordance with IEC 61851-1, IEC 61851-21 and IEC 61851-
22.

(14) The safety provisions of all DC charging stations shall
be in accordance with IEC 61851-1, IEC 61851-21, IEC 61851-23
and IEC 61851-24.

(15) All charging stations shall have the insulation resistance
value as per the manufacturer’s instructions or specifications or as
stipulated in the relevant IEC 61851-1 standard.

(16) Electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) shall not create
faults (typically through a circuit breaker or overcurrent protection),
harmonics, and frequency imbalance in the distribution network.

(17) Any person who contravenes this section shall be guilty of
an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 5 or to imprisonment
for a period not exceeding six months or to both such fine and such
imprisonment.
Periodic assessment of electric vehicle charging stations

7. (1) Every EV charging station owned, operated or managed by
any operator must be subject to periodic assessment commencing on
or before the first anniversary of connection of that charging station to
a supply of electricity.
S.I. 120 of 2026
1713

(2) Subsequent periodic assessments must take place at
intervals of no more than twelve months.

(3) An EV charging station or EVSE must immediately be
taken out of service by the electric vehicle charging station operator
if the periodic assessment has not been carried out within twelve
months from the date of first installation, or within twelve months
from the date of the last inspection for that EV charging station.

(4) An EV charging station must be taken out of service
immediately by the electric vehicle charging station operator if found
to be unsafe at any time by any person, or in the event of an electric
shock that results in a person being admitted to hospital.

(5) An EV charging station taken out of service in accordance
with this section cannot be reconnected until its safety has been
confirmed, following repair, and a new periodic assessment issued.

(6) An electric vehicle charging station operator must—

(a)	 establish and implement a safety assessment programme
(periodic assessment) for regularly assessing the
electrical safety of EVSE, conductors and fittings; and

(b)	 keep records of—

(i)	 the results of every periodic assessment; and

(ii)	 details of any issues found during the assessment; and

(iii)	 any actions required to be taken in relation to those
issues; and

(c)	 retain a copy of these records, whether in hard copy or
electronically, for at least five years; and

(d)	 on request, provide a copy of the records to the Authority
within ten working days after the request.

(7) EVSE shall be capable of providing a technical basis for
billing options, metering accuracy, and network connectivity.

(8) EVSE shall be capable of upgrades to enable smart-grid-
capability through Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP) transmission.

(9) Any person who contravenes this section shall be guilty of
an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 5 or to imprisonment

Electricity (Electric Vehicle Charging Station Safety) Regulations, 2026
for a period not exceeding six months or to both such fine and such
imprisonment.
Electrical safety for users, equipment, and infrastructure

8. (1) No person may charge an electric vehicle by any, or any
combination, of the following means—

(a)	 use of any EV plug adaptor that is not designed and
approved by the EVSE manufacturer; or

(b)	 use of any EV adaptor that is not designed and approved
by the car manufacturer and approved by the EVSE
manufacturer; or

(c)	 cascading of two or more supply leads; or

(d)	 use of an extension lead; or

(e)	 use of a socket-outlet for the supply of more than one
vehicle at a time; or

(f)
use of an EVSE that is originally labelled by the
manufacturer indicating it is not compatible with the
230V or 380V and 50Hz; or

(g) 	 use of two or more connecting points to charge the same
EV.

(2) No person may supply electricity for EV charging of an
electric vehicle other than through a charging station.

(3) Any person who contravenes this section shall be guilty of
an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 5 or to imprisonment
for a period not exceeding six months or to both such fine and such
imprisonment.
Electricity sources integration

9. (1) Where more than two electricity sources are interfaced for
the purpose of supplying electricity to the charging station, the electricity
sources shall be interfaced through a changeover switch.

(2) The changeover switch shall indicate the electricity source
that will be powering at any given time.

(2) Any person who contravenes this section shall be guilty of

Signage and information

11. (1) EV charging stations, other than in residential use, shall
have posted signage, allowing only EVs to park in such charging spaces.

(2) 	 EV charging stations shall have the following information
affixed—

(a)	 outlet options;

(b) Voltage and amperage levels;

(c) time of use and fees; and

(d) safety information.
Power of enforcement

12. The Authority shall have the power to obtain, remove and test
any EV charging station to enforce compliance with these regulations.
